quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out so the group is easier to see.
Stay close together so the group is easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so the group is easier to see.
questions.explanation: Staying close together makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Each rider still needs enough space to move safely. Riding in pairs does not give riders enough room to move.

questions.question: What should you do on a long trip?

options.text: Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take breaks at least every 2 hours. Do not use caffeine because you will become very tired when it wears off.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard ahead
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals that there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use quiet roads with less traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use quiet roads with less traffic.
questions.explanation: You can help by arranging other transportation, getting friends to help stop them, and slowing their drinking. Do not tell them to drive on quiet roads. Someone who has been drinking should not drive at all, no matter what roads they use.

questions.question: During the day, what should you do with your headlight?

options.text: Switch between high and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not behind or heading toward other vehicles.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly, reduce how much you lean, and then press harder on the brakes as you slow down.

questions.question: What causes nearly half of all motorcycle crash deaths?
questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol use
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of fatal motorcycle crashes. Studies show that 40 to 45 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what is best?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out. Your path may not follow the curve exactly.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what should you do with your headlight?

options.text: Switch between high and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What happens if you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When leaning into a turn, your tires use some grip to make the turn. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: On a paved two-lane road, where do sand and gravel collect most?

options.text: Near the center of the road.
Near the sides of the road.
In the center of each lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Sand and gravel collect on the sides of roads, especially on curves and on-ramps and off-ramps. Be extra careful when riding over loose dirt and gravel.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. If the left arm is bent at the elbow and points down, it means the rider is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep riders cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep riders cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket prevents dehydration and protects you. Many jackets are designed to keep riders cool, even when it is hot outside.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always worst. Choose your lane position based on the riding conditions.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When the road is wet, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center part of the lane
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of the lane. This creates a slippery strip. When the road is wet, this strip becomes dangerous. You can usually move to the side of this strip and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar, why should you not ride too far right?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will have trouble passing other vehicles.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is on the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far right, the sidecar may go off the road. The same is true for the right rear wheel on a three-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which changes how your motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. Brake light position does not need to be adjusted.
